¡Hola Chicos!

Les escribe el profesor Yair Chico Vence, docente de física y estadística del colegio Jerusalem de Barranquilla, los invito a formar parte del equipo Gamma del semillero SICE Jerusalem y que vivan una super experiencia durante el Desafío de aplicaciones especiales de la Nasa 2026.
summary: "What was left behind" is a cinematic short film that honors the silent sentinels of human space exploration. Through a compelling narrative and ultra-realistic visuals, it tells the story of a dedicated team of researchers on Earth monitoring the final transmissions of abandoned rovers and probes like Viking, Sojourner, Kepler, and Pioneer, highlighting their legacy in the vast, hostile universe.
details:
2. The Problem We Are Solving

Space exploration is often viewed purely through cold data and engineering. We forget the emotional and historical weight of the machines we leave behind. The challenge was to communicate the profound legacy of our robotic pioneers to a general audience, transforming technical history into an inspiring, awe-striking cinematic experience that connects humanity with its metallic ambassadors drifting in deep space.

3. Our Solution We produced a high-quality cinematic short film in record time that blends real aerospace history with artistic storytelling. Our narrative follows a team of NASA researchers who monitor these distant machines.

  • The Narrative: We scripted an emotionally driven story highlighting real missions (the Viking landers, the Sojourner rover on Mars, the drifting Kepler Space Telescope, and the Pioneer probes sailing into the galactic ocean).
  • The Execution: Through rapid video editing, precise camera direction, and immersive lighting, we brought the isolation of space to life. The film acts as a "message in a bottle," reminding viewers that long after these probes lose power, they will remain as monuments of human curiosity.

4. How We Used Space Agency Data / Concepts Our script and visual direction were heavily based on real mission statuses and locations:

  • Mars Rovers: Historical data on Viking 1 & 2 and the Sojourner rover's final resting places.
  • Deep Space Probes: Trajectory and operational status of Pioneer 10 and 11 crossing the borders of our solar system.
  • Telescopes: The current Earth-trailing orbit of the decommissioned Kepler Space Telescope.

5. The Team (Space Apps Roster)

  • Ramiro Martinez: Lead NASA Researcher, Video Editor & Scriptwriter.
  • Camilo Salas: Astronaut Performance & Camera Direction.
  • Gaby: Rover Researcher & Data Monitor.
  • Majo & Isabella Paez: Research Specialists.
  • Jose: Lighting Design & Atmospheric Ambiance.
